trajectory_summary: A low-friction, procedurally complete call: verify items, qualifiers, and bill collection all landed, and a specific appointment time was locked with the bill in hand. Energy stayed flat throughout — the customer never expressed real bill pain or curiosity, and the rep never tried to create any, running the script as a checklist rather than building toward an anchored close.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Friday) and time (6PM) were mutually agreed, and the bill was received on the call, satisfying the appointment conditions; no co-owner was identified since the customer stated no one else is on the title.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The $180 bill was captured at 02:16 but the rep immediately diverted into a meter-wiring tangent instead of flipping it into pain/urgency; the flip should have landed right after the bill number, e.g. tying it to 'that's exactly the kind of bill our program targets.'

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep requested the utility bill at 03:37 and the customer said they'd text it; the rep confirmed receipt on the call at 06:45.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The stated reason ('just trying to get an estimate') was never referenced again when setting or confirming the appointment — a missed chance to tie the appointment explicitly to getting that estimate.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Bill captured but never flipped into urgency
primary_coaching_focus.why: The single biggest anchor available on this call (a monthly bill amount) was filed and never used to build a reason to show up — classic capture-without-flip per coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring.

key_moments.quote: Just trying to get an estimate to be honest.
key_moments.stewart_read: The interest reason was thin and the rep took it at face value without probing depth — no bill-pain or motivation was ever surfaced.

key_moments.stewart_read: Bill amount was captured but the rep pivoted immediately into an unrelated meter-wiring tangent rather than reflecting the bill back as a hook.

key_moments.stewart_read: A brand-new roof removes a common objection/DQ risk and is a positive qualification signal the rep captured but did not reinforce as a plus for the customer.
